title: Window frames: `RANGE … CURRENT ROW` with an order, the whole partition without
verdict: `default_window_frame`: SQL's; `lag`, `lead`, `nth_value` as SQL; ties in arrival order
description: Without a frame, a window with `ORDER BY` uses `RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW`, so peers are included (`sum` over keys 1, 2, 2, 3 gives 10, 60, 60, 100, and `last_value` is the last peer); without `ORDER BY` the frame is the whole partition. `lag`, `lead` take a default; `nth_value(x, 2)` is NULL until the frame has two rows and takes `IGNORE NULLS`. A `RANGE` frame over doubles treats NaN as a peer of NaN only.
Ties in the window order get the order the rows arrive in: `row_number() OVER (ORDER BY g)` after a 3-way shuffle numbered ids 2, 10, 4, 8, 6, 0 for `g = 0`.
reference: `lag`, `lead`, `first_value` and windowed aggregates over the window's order and frame; ties in any order (`tie_order`). Spark is native.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: with `ORDER BY` and no frame the plan shows `RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW`; running `sum` and `last` per partition
`last(four) OVER (ORDER BY ten)` gives 2 on all three rows with ten = 0: the frame includes peers
without `ORDER BY` the frame is `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING`, the whole partition
`lead(ten * 2, 1, -1)` gives the default -1 past the partition's end
`nth_value(employee_name, 2)` is NULL on the first row, then the second-highest
`nth_value(v, n) IGNORE NULLS` over a `RANGE` frame skips NULLs: NULL until n non-NULL values
two tied rows (cate a, val 1) both get count 2 and sum 2 under the default frame

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.
